source_rows.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use Standard Precautions when infection is known or suspected, then add Transmission-Based Precautions if the organism requires them.","B":"Use Standard Precautions for tasks with anticipated blood or body-fluid exposure, but not for routine noninvasive bedside care.","C":"Use Standard Precautions routinely in inpatient units, while outpatient settings rely mainly on diagnosis-specific precautions.","D":"Use them for every client, selecting hand hygiene and task-based PPE according to anticipated exposure."}}

source_rows.rationale: ACOG explains that lying flat in later pregnancy can allow the gravid uterus to compress a major vessel, reducing venous return and causing dizziness; turning to either side relieves the positional compression. Option B directly addresses the likely mechanism. Option A maintains the provoking position. Option C assumes hypoglycemia without evidence and does not first correct the positional cause. Option D delays the needed repositioning while the client remains symptomatic.
